prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a close, downward-looking layout: the camera wearer’s red-sleeved arm and the lower foreground are nearest, roughly 0.1–0.5 m away, while the reclining person and bedding extend across the middle and upper image at roughly 0.5–1.5 m. The other person remains in front of and mostly to the right of the wearer, with their phone resting only about 0.1–0.3 m from their torso; the wearer’s reaching hand comes within roughly 0.2–0.5 m of the person or nearby bedding. Across the five frames, the foreground arm shifts rightward and then upward toward the other person, while the other person stays at broadly similar depth and becomes more fully visible as the camera turns right. Depth makes near-versus-far layering and the separation of overlapping limbs and bedding clearer than RGB, but its smooth surfaces, missing fine boundaries, and unstable brightness around arms, hair, and image edges make metre estimates approximate.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map supports object-level layout by separating people, the bed or bedding, and a possible teddy bear: large person masks occupy the upper and central view, while the wearer’s partly visible body or arm enters from the lower and left foreground. It indicates that the reclining person is in front of the wearer at about 0.5–1.2 m, with overlapping bodies or limbs much closer to each other—often within arm’s reach—and with substantial portions cut off by the frame. Across the strip, masks change from several separated person regions to large merged regions as the camera and foreground arm move right, while the bed remains behind or beneath them. This map makes occlusion boundaries and object occupancy easier to see than RGB, but the labels and instances are unreliable: person regions merge with bedding, the apparent teddy-bear and bed labels are inconsistent, and some foreground objects or body parts are omitted or assigned changing classes.
descriptions.pose: The pose map provides almost no usable body geometry in the first three frames, then detects a magenta hand near the upper-right area in frames four and five. In RGB context, that hand is roughly 0.5–1.0 m in front of the camera wearer and close to the reclining person’s upper body, moving farther right between the last two frames while remaining within that person’s arm’s reach. No body skeleton, head orientation, gaze direction, or reliable facing direction is recovered, so the map cannot establish whether either person looks toward the wearer; most bodies are also partly outside the view or occluded. The hand landmarks reveal finger and palm configuration that is hard to isolate in RGB, but the sparse detections and complete absence of the wearer’s prominent foreground arm make this map highly unreliable for the overall scene layout.
